We visited the Royal Botanical Gardens in Kandy, a sprawling 147-acre expanse that dates back to the 14th century, though its formal establishment was in 1821. We only had time to explore a small portion, perhaps two or three acres, but were captivated by its beauty. The gardens are world-renowned for their extensive collection of over 4,000 plant species, including a magnificent orchid house, spices, medicinal plants, and imposing palm avenues. A unique feature is the tradition of visiting dignitaries planting memorial trees; one notable example is the Ceylon ironwood tree planted by Tsar Nicholas II of Russia during his visit in 1891.

Its well signposted and you can pick where you want to roam. The only place that was disappointing was the conservatory - seemed neglected and plants were not at all exciting.

Just 15 minutes from Kandy city, the Royal Botanic Gardens, Peradeniya is a must-visit for anyone who loves nature, photography, or simply a peaceful stroll. The gardens are huge and beautifully maintained, with over 4,000 plant species from around the world. My favourites were the colourful Orchid House, the impressive avenue of Royal Palms, and the massive Javan fig tree which is truly a wonder to see. It’s a very calm and relaxing place, with plenty of benches to sit and take in the scenery. You can easily spend 2–3 hours wandering here. Tip: Visit in the morning or late afternoon for softer light and fewer crowds. Wear comfortable shoes as the gardens are quite big, and bring your camera — every corner is a photo opportunity!

The origins of the Botanic Gardens date as far back as 1371 when King Wickramabahu III ascended the throne and kept court at Peradeniya near the Mahaweli river. This was followed by King Kirti Sri and King Rajadhi Rajasinghe. A temple was built on this location by King Wimala Dharma, but it was destroyed by the British when they were given control over the Kingdom of Kandy.[citation needed] Thereafter, the groundwork for a botanical garden was formed by Alexandar Moon in 1821. He used the garden for coffee and cinnamon plants.[4] The Botanical Garden at Peradeniya was formally established in 1843 with plants brought from Kew Garden, Slave Island, Colombo, and the Kalutara Garden in Kalutara. The Royal Botanic Garden, Peradeniya was made more independent and expanded under George Gardner as superintendent in 1844. On Gardner's death in 1849 George Henry Kendrick Thwaites became superintendent. He served until he resigned in 1879, when he was succeeded by Henry Trimen, who served until 1895.[5][6] He was succeeded in turn by John Christopher Willis who served as director from 1898 until 1912. The garden came under the administration of the Department of Agriculture when it was established in 1912. There are avenues in the River Drive such as Cook's Pine Avenue, Palmyra Palm Avenue, Double Coconut Avenue, Cabbage Palm Avenue, and Royal Palm Avenue.[7] The classical Avenue of Palms is in this Garden. One item with a significant history is the Cannonball Tree planted by King George V of the United Kingdom and Queen Mary in 1901. It is often load with fruit, which are thought to resemble cannonballs. During World War II, the Botanic Garden was used by Lord Louis Mountbatten, the supreme commander of the allied forces in the South Asia, as the headquarters of the South East Asia Command. The gardens were used as a location in the 1957 film The Bridge on the River Kwai. We visited Peradeniya Botanical Gardens in April with our family, and it was truly one of the highlights of our trip to Kandy. The gardens are vast, beautifully maintained, and offer a perfect blend of natural beauty and tranquility. Walking through the towering palm avenues, orchid house, and spice gardens was a relaxing and enriching experience. The sheer variety of flora was impressive, and the kids especially enjoyed the giant bamboo and the massive Javan fig tree. The weather in April was warm but pleasant, and there were plenty of shaded areas to rest. We packed some snacks and had a lovely little picnic on the grass. It’s also a great spot for photography—every corner has something unique to offer. Highly recommend this place for families, nature lovers, or anyone looking to spend a peaceful day outdoors. Give yourself at least 2–3 hours to explore fully. Tip: Wear comfortable shoes, bring water, and try to visit early in the morning or late afternoon to avoid the midday heat.

Explanatory stands with interesting information have been set up. They give you a map at the entrance. We've had some bad luck with the weather, but on a sunny day it should be really nice.

This was day three of our stay in Sri Lanka and what a way to start the set of excursions we had planned. We had no idea how amazing this set of gardens were going to be. The plants, trees, colours, shrubs were simply stunning in colour. We walked for about 2.5 hours and could easily have been there for longer. Our guide walked with us and told us of the tradition for the benches in the park where ladies sit and meet their male partners or meet a male partner. It was so lovely to see so many young couples sitting and starting out on their life’s journey. Lord Mountbatten’s World War II residence is in the grounds as is the famous tree shown in the film The Bridge Over the River Kwai. We finished up at one of the cares with cold ginger beers and lemonade’s. What an amazing place and one you must see if you are in Kandy.

If you like your botany with a side order of Colonial history, and movie trivia, Kandy Botanical Gardens will suit you down to the ground! These gardens, a former Royal Garden dating back to the 14th century, are beautifully laid out but not in an overly formal style. The British turned it into a Botanical Garden in the19th century. A highlight of the visit was a guided tour led by Mr Bandara Palipana, the lead academic for the gardens and author of numerous books on the gardens and the flora of Sri Lanka (he will happily sell you one from a bundle he carries around with him!). Mr Palipana, a distinguished,older gentleman, full of anecdotes, took us on a tour of superlatives, showing us the oldest, biggest, most poisonous, most important, most beautiful, most beneficial, trees and plants. He also regaled us with tales of Royal visits by HM Queen Elizabeth and Lord Mountbatten who lived in a bungalow in the grounds, and the garden's role in the movie 'Bridge Over The River Kwai'. All in all, an absolute treat!.

The Royal Botanical Garden in Peradeniya, Kandy, is one of the most desirable places on the island. It is home to more than 13,000 different species of plants, some unique to the island itself. A place to truly desire mother nature and to spend quality time with your loved ones

It is a fantastic beautiful and well-maintained garden with a large number of different trees, palms, bushes and plants. There is also a lilies restaurant (Royal Botanical Cafeteria) that serves a small buffet but it is not the one you should visit the garden for.

We visited as part of a Sri Lanka Tour (and to pass time before something else).

Absolutely stunning. Incredible variety, so well maintained. And it's huge! You could easily make a full day of it here. Every single area we visited was lovely. The entire place is 147 acres, so it can be tiring traversing the place on foot, but we went at a leisurely pace and were able to cover much of it, even alongside my elderly father. Funnily enough, when we purchased the tickets he balked at the price ("3000 rupees?! That's outrageous!") but by the end of it he was more than satisfied, and said himself it was well worth it! There are carts for rent if you don't want to walk the entire area (understandable!) and multiple options for food and drinks. Definitely worth the time and money, especially if you have family members who are uninterested or can't do activities like hiking, etc.

a beautiful place with many amazing plants and trees to discover. Sadly when we visited we struggled to walk the entire area, there were buggys to hire but they were all out. The orchid house is beautiful and has many different species of orchid and the huge palm trees are magnificent There were plenty of monkeys enjoying the gardens too which only added to the trip there They have a nice shop on the site and gifts were reasonably priced

This isn't my usual field of interest, but we enjoyed it so much. We hired a golf cart to take us around, and the driver was so knowledgeable and entertaining. It's a lovely way to spend a few hours in the shade and quiet. The garden is huge and so we'll maintained. I love seing the aquirels and fruitbats especially

A beautifully kept garden with delights around every corner. Exotic flowers and towering trees. Near a busy  road and with a stream of people entering we were surprised to  find areas where we were alone and there was silence. 3000 Rupees to enter for foreigners. One can hire a golf buggy to be driven around if mobility is poor. We enjoyed the topiary hedges, there was a deserted maze, orchid house, rose garden and so much more we did not  have time to see. Many birds we haven’t seen anywhere else , monkeys, bats and a mongoose. Allow two to three hours. Toilets are dire.

The Royal Botanic Gardens at Peradeniya was established in 1821, six years after the final occupation of the Kandyan Kingdom by the English. The site is less than 5.5 Km from Kandy on the Colombo Road, and occupies a loop of the river Mahaweli, which surrounds it on all sides except the south, where it is bounded by the main road. The area 61.25 ha in extent, is about 1550ft from sea level. More than 4000 species of plants including woody trees, Palms, Ferns, Orchids and shrubs currently present within the gardens.

Peradeniya Botanical Garden is a must-visit for nature lovers. The sprawling grounds are filled with historical trees, stunning flowers, and inviting lawns. While the entry fee for foreigners (3000 LKR) is significantly higher than for locals (200 LKR), the experience is well worth it. Just be mindful of the monkeys that can be found in certain areas and take necessary precautions to avoid any unwanted encounters. Overall, Peradeniya Botanical Garden offers a peaceful and enchanting escape from the hustle and bustle of the city.

Botanical Gardens of Peradeniya - 147 acres in extent, this is the best and the largest garden in Sri Lanka that a visitor to Kandy should never miss. Created in the 14th Century as the Pleasure Garden of Kandyan Kings, the Royal Botanical Gardens of Peradeniya is surrounded by the river Mahaweli on three sides and is connected to the opposite bank by a suspension bridge. With more than 4000 species of flora, the garden is an example of the wealth and beauty of the tropics. With more than hundred varieties of palm trees, five palm avenues where palms such as Talipot grow to an immense size, wonderful arches of glossy foliage, lovely fernery, and orchid houses with rare blossoms and spice trees in groves make it a rich botanical heritage in the world.

As a seasoned tour guide with over a decade of experience in showcasing the best of Sri Lanka, the Peradeniya Botanical Garden remains one of my favorite places to take visitors. This sprawling garden, nestled near Kandy, is a haven for nature lovers and offers a unique glimpse into the island’s rich botanical heritage.

The alley of palm trees and giant water lilies are something incredible. The place is ideal for cool photos and videos. A real paradise for everyone who loves nature and beauty!

Beautiful site from start to finish. Unfortunately we could not get an electric car to tour the park, and did most of 63 acres of it on foot in 35 degree heat. However, the majestic trees provide much needed shade and it did not seem too strenuous after all. Many trees have been planted by dignitaries of times past, such as King George and Queen Mary of England in 1901. Queen Elizabeth II also visited twice, in 1954 and in 1981. We found the experience very fulfilling and learned about many previously unknown trees and plants. Monkeys add a funny aspect to the experience. Just mind you don’t leave your bag on the floor. Very good toilet facilities. Highly recommended.

Tourism in Sri Lanka is being affected by a disappointing two-tier system that shows no respect for foreign visitors at attractions, 3000rs for foreigners and a fraction of the price for locals. As someone who has visited many botanical gardens, I must say that this one is mediocre at best. The only highlight for me was watching the fruit bats.

Peradeniya Botanical Garden is a must-visit destination for nature enthusiasts and anyone seeking tranquility amidst lush greenery. Walking through its sprawling grounds, you're greeted with a mesmerizing array of exotic plants and trees from around the world. The meticulously curated pathways lead you on a journey through different ecosystems, from towering palm trees to vibrant orchid displays. One of the highlights is the majestic avenue of royal palms, a breathtaking sight that evokes a sense of grandeur. The variety of flora is astounding, with each section offering something new to discover. The orchid house is a particular delight, showcasing rare and colorful blooms in a serene setting. Beyond its botanical wonders, Peradeniya Botanical Garden offers a peaceful escape from the hustle and bustle of everyday life. Whether you're strolling along the tranquil riverbanks or picnicking beneath the shade of ancient trees, there's a sense of serenity that envelops you. The garden is well-maintained, and the staff are friendly and knowledgeable, eager to share insights about the plants and their origins. Additionally, the visitor facilities are clean and convenient, making for a pleasant overall experience. Overall, Peradeniya Botanical Garden is a true gem, offering a harmonious blend of natural beauty and relaxation. Whether you're a nature lover, a photographer, or simply looking for a peaceful retreat, this botanical paradise is sure to leave a lasting impression.

The first time we fell for it thinking this guy had something valid to tell us about the tree.  The second and third time just politely declined.  But all over the park we saw other tourists being conned in the same way.  Being led down the paths away from the main path.  Not only do you pay considerably more to get in than local people, you are then extorted by the workers once inside.  Beware

Views from the suspension bridge are fantastic as well as interesting engineering construction.

We had a very enjoyable visit to the Royal Botanic Gardens. Kandy City can be noisy and quite polluted, so it was nice to get away to the gardens for some peace and clean air. The gardens are beautifully maintained and have a very relaxed feel. You are provided with a good map when you get your tickets and that is very useful to plan your route. Most impressive are probably the coconut palms. At the far end of the garden there is a wobbly suspension bridge out over the Mahaweli River, which is worth a walk on! There are also a large number of trees around the Great Circle planted by world leaders and royalty over the years, which is nice to see. All in all, a good place to spend a couple of hours.

This is Sri Lanka's main botanical gardens; as such we expected more (especially having see the equivalent in other Asian countries such as Singapore). Sri Lanka has a vast range of "exotic" plants native to the country - thus you would expect the botanical gardens to display them to the full - put simply, it doesn't. Well worth visiting, and well looked after.

Beautifully kept, very well laid out gardens with many species of trees, plants, shrubs and grasses. Giant Bamboos, many varieties of palms, huge trees. Tree lined avenues and riverside walk. Nice way to enjoy 2hrs relaxing in the open air.

I visited here in December. The weather was nice and the gardens were beautiful! There were a wide variety of vegetation, including lots of tall trees, and very pretty plants. There were also lots of monkeys chilling around the place. There are bats too, you can hear them up in the trees. They are big bats, but I was told they are vegetarians. The grounds had lots of families and couples hanging about but it def did not feel crowded. There are bathrooms in the garden and they seem sanitary. Highly recommend!

This place was simply amazing. So much natural beauty on display. We managed to spend over 5hrs in here. You could do it faster but we could have easily spent more time here. Staff are really friendly throughout the gardens and we got pulled aside quite a few times for them to point out things. They seemed to take a very keen interest in making sure visitors saw things they might otherwise miss. Huge colony of fruit bats was pointed out to us. Troops of Toque macaques abound, plenty of magnificent birds and amazing displays of colour from the flowers. In some areas the scent of the flowers was quite heady. Restaurant on site we didn't try but the shop next to it selling drinks and snacks was really good value considering we were a captive audience. Probably our best value day in Kandy and quite possibly my favourite attraction. Highly recommended

They are very interesting if you have a guide who explains the different types of trees and plants. The greenhouse with the orchids and the avenues of Coco de Mer are wonderful. Then a multitude of specialist plant houses and flower beds. Simply stunning

Peradeniya Botanic Gardens is a unique gift of Mother Nature with its ancient yet beautiful landscape.  This garden will be of great use to biologists, as it is home to a wide variety of species. One of the oldest botanical gardens in the world.  Our guide around the gardens was the botanist Bandara Palipana and he made it a most interesting tour.  We saw many trees and shrubs which were new to us and the stories behind some of the plantings was interesting.  The orchis collection has over 300 varieties on show.  The Cook pine (introduced from New Caledonia by Captain Cook) is unusual as always leans towards the equator.   HM Queen Elizabeth II, Lord Mountbatten, King George IV, Yuri Gagarin and others have planted trees there.  Lord Mountbatten used the old residence in the centre f the park as his headquarters as Supreme Allied Commander of South East Asia Command during WWII.  The gardens are kept in a pristine condition.  Many Bollywood films have used it for location shooting.

The glowing reviews of the Botanical Garden baffle me.  Yes, it’s beautifully laid out, but labeling is miserable.  Upon entry, paying the massive foreigners’ fee – as if we’re some sort of different animal from Sri Lankans – visitors are given a map with such tiny print that it’s almost impossible to see.  The roads/paths aren’t marked on the map, and there’s no indication of the location of the flora featured on the pages adjacent to the map.  Some plants are labeled; most are not.  And the labels are pretty useless.  A large plot of dahlias, for example, are simply described as dahlias, no indication of the specific cross or the name of each plant.  It’s even worse in the orchid house, where the labels that would indicate the cross of the orchids, even the species name, are neatly hidden, and visitors are specifically admonished not to touch the plant labels.  So in the end the Botanical Garden offers a lovely stroll in an otherwise crowded city, but informative it most certainly is not.

Although my wife and are lovers of all things historical, occasionally we need to refresh the mind and relax. The Gardens were included on our tour itinerary and provided a welcome interlude from the intensity of the UNESCO sites. The origins of the Gardens date to 1371 and they were declared a Royal Garden during the reign of King Kirti Sri Rajasinghe between 1747 - 1780. The Gardens on their present site were established in 1821 and cover an area of 60ha. showcasing over 4,000 species. The informative guide map that we received on entry contained a detailed legend and history of the Gardens. We spent approx. three hours strolling the walkways and admiring the beauty of the flora and it's diversity. The Orchid House held a marvelous display and variety of exotic blooms. We enjoyed the Flower garden with many annuals and perennials in bloom. The Palm Avenues are spectacular and include Royal, Cabbage and  Palmyrah, not to be ignored and great for photos, especially the Coco de Mer of Seychelles notoriety. We saw some of the tallest grasses in the world, stands of bamboos on River Drive, including the giant bamboo of Burma. We enjoyed the Fernery, Spice Garden, Cacti and the Arboretum. Interesting plaques recognizing world leaders and renowned visitors who planted trees there. Lovely way to spend a morning and then adjourn to the pleasant café near the entrance.

Well worth going and spending half day here. There are less flowers in the gardens than I expected and the gardens are dominated by large trees, with some particularly impressive specimens. There are also large collections of Bamboo and palms. There is also a reasonably nice orchid house. I think I was most impressed by the large number of flying foxes (bats) that roost in the trees in the corner near the suspension bridge. There are thousands, and the information board says 24k which I can believe. They make quite a racket, and you do see quite a number flying around which is impressive as they are huge. One minor critism is that there were too few benches, and those that were available were always occupied by courting couples, it seems to be where they come. Overall a great place to spend a few hours, although not in the same league as other  botantical gardens such as the one in Singapore which is a lot bigger with a vastly superior collection of orchids.

Great day out with my clients. It was very peaceful and relaxing to walk around. You can hire a buggy there itself if you want to see it all within limited time. One of the nicest green spaces i've ever experienced Just a quick glance at all the trip advisor reviews on here and its obvious the botanical gardens are popular and highly rated. I can only add weight to that and say that we thoroughly enjoyed spending an afternoon here, though you could spend a full day if you had the time. We were contemplating just having a rest day round the pool at the hotel but decided to make the journey here and we were SO glad we did. Other places should look to this place as an example of a well thought out, maintained and looked after urban green space. It contains a bewildering variety of plants and trees, giant fruit bats hanging from and flying between the trees, monkeys you can get right up close to, lakes, and an orchid house with some of the most amazing flowers. There is a cafe / buffet restaurant in the park, but this would make a lovely place to bring a picnic. If you appreciate and enjoy nature and green spaces then this is a must visit if staying in or near Kandy. It is approx. 15 mins from Kandy city to here by tuk tuk and the fare should cost about 5 GBP. If you have already been on a tuk tuk with a mad driver then you will understand what an 'experience' this is, and if you haven't then do try to experience this at least once in your travels !

After a long period of non-stop rain, we headed out to the Botanical Gardens in a tuk tuk with our fingers crossed that it wouldn't be a complete washout. The place turned out to be far better than we'd have dared to hope. The entrance fee of 1500 rupees (about £7) for foreigners is not cheap - but nothing in Kandy worth seeing seems to be cheap. I would say though that it was absolutely worth it. The site is enormous with a spectacular diversity of plants and trees and lots to see and do. The map was a bit rubbish as it didn't really suggest any sensible way to tackle the gardens, so we just blundered about a bit, saving the orchid house until last and focusing first on the outdoor areas just in case the rain came back. We had lunch at the cafeteria beside the Great Lawn, watching hundreds of children playing tag during their lunch break. The food at the cafeteria was surprisingly good value for such a 'captive audience' kind of place - we had a fish curry set meal including soup and fruit salad plus a lime soda each and it was about 2000 rupees for more food than we could eat. The fern house was a bit of a health and safety trap with tools and hoses left out all over the place but everything else was in good working order. We got a bus back to the city for just 20 rupees each after we left. The bus stops are to the left of the entrance. Tuk Tuks were asking 500. Just ask if the bus goes to the clock tower or central market.

Well worth a visit although the entry price is a bit steep for foreigners - 1500LKR per person. The orchid house displayed some beautiful orchids and there were other lovely gardens, cafes and restaurants and plenty of open spaces and shade. We took around 2 hours to explore and have some lunch, and would have spent more time were it not so hot.

I didn’t think I would enjoy a walk through a Botanical Garden, especially in the heat but was delighted with our walk around the gardens.  Our driver said about two hours would do it we only took an hour and enjoyed it immensely.  Not long after walking into the gardens a snake slithered across our path with my husband nearly stepping on it, gave us a fright.  The gardens were beautiful and I actually saw several types of trees I had never seen before.  The monkeys were different to others we had seen with a big red face.  A friendly Gardener approached for a chat and then of course wanted a tip.

Nice place to escape the busy town of Kandy. It was nice to walk around and well maintained. Also pleasant to stop for a cup of Ceylon tea and an ice cream in the tea house. Display houses not so good and man who told us a few things wanted a tip!!

A really beautiful, expansive, well laid out garden.  Perfect Eden just out of the main city. Informative reading material and map provided at the ticket office. Pleasant restaurant by the main green for lunch and drinks. We spent a wonderful few hours here strolling along the various avenues of plants and trees. A highlight of our stay in Kandy.

It’s a lovely garden with maintained place, plenty of interesting trees to see and knowledge. The orchid house is wonderful. There is a shop if you want to relax and have a cup of coffee. You can simply spend 2 hours to cover all the places. I would like to recommend this place if you can walk long if not you can hire a small car inside the garden.

It's a favorite among the locals and you'll see a whole lot of kids, couples, families coming in for picnics, strolls and spending some quiet time. Would absolutely recommend comfortable footwear. The orchids were nothing to die for but decently maintained. Worth a visit

Its a nice garden with lots of interesting trees to see and experience such as, double coconut (never heard of it before), giant bamboo tree, 25 varietes of grass. The orchid house is nice with some very delightful species. However the display is not as tastefully done as one would see in places like Singapore or Netherlands. We had to hire a buggy as I was travelling with my elderly parents who would have found it hard to walk the entire length. With the help of the buggy, we saw the garden in an hour. It was handy to have the buggy (which cost 2000 LKR + 500LKR as tip for the driver) as it had started raining heavily while we were still on the rounds. There is a small gift shop and a barrista coffee place too if needed.

If time is short then I would recommend hiring buggy with driver. Buggy seets 7 and costs LKR2000 plus LKR500 tip for driver who doubles as commentator & photographer.  It takes 1 hour & allows you to see most of the garden. Particularly useful if weather is too humid.

The Gardens are probably 5km from Kandy, a short Tuk tuk ride. We spent around 3 hours walking around the Gardens. They are beautifully kept and the Trees are spectacular. The clumps of bamboos add to beauty of the Park as do the plants and the river. In one corner of the Gardens 20 plus thousand fruit bats roost which is a spectacular sight. There are places to take refreshments. I would highly recommend a visit.

We had a one hour guided tour of the gardens. Our guide was very informative and we loved the beautiful surrounds; magnificent trees and avenues, flowers and lawned areas all beautiful set out. Loved the history and the trees planted by notables such as King George V. Definitely worth a visit.

You all must visit this location to spend your day , it's very peaceful and beautiful location , kids can play with the environment , the garden is big , if you walk all along the way , it will take 4-5 hours, there are lot of places to take beautiful photos. Skip raining days

We spent a couple of hours here en route elsewhere, but we could have spent far longer! Lots to see and many fascinating and unusual plants, all clearly labelled. The orchid house was stunning, so many different colours and shapes. Wonderful palm walk, and a fascinating “cannon ball” tree! Tranquil areas for wandering, but also lots of grassy spaces for family games and local wedding photos - as it was the weeeknd when we visited, there was lots happening which gave a lovely insight to Sri Lankan everyday life! There’s also ponds, lakes and even a rope style suspension bridge, which gives great views over the river. Sadly the fruit bats we’d hoped to see weren’t in evidence, but it was a very enjoyable visit indeed!

Visited here whilst in Kandy for the day and loved the place. We took a leisurely stroll down the main path to the green, down palm avenue to the suspension bridge, taken in the orchid house on route. Suspension bridge was fun to walk across but not quite sure why there is a gate in the middle with a sign that states stop. We saw some people get to the gate and turn round and then some people got to the gate and opened it and walked all the way across! Then walked along the side of the river and back round to the main entrance. At a leisurely pace this took about an hour. Nice little cafe by the entrance where I enjoyed a great milkshake. Great gift shop with some lovely items reasonably priced.

Enter the gardens by the back entrance, if possible, so that you can cross the river by rope bridge which makes the experience all the more memorable. The gardens are beautiful and are a lovely place to spend a few hours. In addition to the multitude of plant species there are hundreds of fruit bats hanging from the trees in certain areas. A really pleasant afternoon.

Spent a couple of hours wandering around the gardens, really quiet even though its in the city, Beautiful flowers and even if you are not a natural gardener it is worth a visit and go for a little walk over the suspension bridge. Also worth watching the monkeys raiding the rubbish bins !

A large botanical gardens given near the centre of Kandy. Would recommend as a way to get some peace in Kandy! It was even possible not to hear the horns when in the middle of the park! There are impressive plants particularly the wild bamboo. Can easily spend a couple of hours.

We were surprised to arrive having to pay an entry fee. Tourist fee is 3000LKR. We enjoyed our walk through the gardens. There are a few paths that are outlined by large palm trees that make for a nice photo. There is also a suspension bridge to go on if you wish which has a nice view of the river. We found that there were minimal benches available to sit on, however this could be due to us visiting on a Sunday where there was a combination of lots of tourist and locals around.

The Royal Botanical Gardens are beautiful and well worth finding time for if you like parks and gardens.  There are monkeys in the park so make sure you have any plastic bags hidden out of view otherwise they will try and take them thinking they contain food.  This happened to us but we kept walking, were followed for a bit and then they left us alone.  We then hid our plastic bag (souvenirs from a spice garden) from view in a fabric bag we had.  It was fine, the monkeys weren’t aggressive so don’t be afraid. We spent two hours there and there was still so much to see. The only disappointing thing about the gardens was the restaurant.  It was mainly a limited range western food and the prices were higher than the city because it is a tourist venue.  You would expect this.  The curry was not available so we ended up having an omelette which came with chips only, and a cheese and ham sandwich which was dry and came with chips and a slightly dry very small salad.  The views over the Great Lawn however were stunning. At 1500Rs it is quite expensive compared to other places but it is worth it. There’s a tuk tuk stand outside if you need it.

We visited on a hot afternoon and wandered the many paths _ there is a map and many signs so it's easy to get around. There are many beautiful old trees some straight out of Lord of the Rings! The sky turned overcast and in the sudden downpour we sheltered in the Orchid House. The suspension bridge barely gets the adrenaline going but is still a laugh.It would be really nice to bring a picnic and sit out in a shady spot.

Great day out. The gardens are beautiful, very well kept and lots of different areas. The orchid house is amazing. There was so many different things to see, it took us about three hours to walk round, facilities good, have a lovely lunch in the pavilion. Also there is a suspension bridge which is worth going over. I would highly recommend a trip here for any nature lovers.

The Botanical Gardens in Kandy are a must visit. Having seen some in India, like the one at Ooty, it is gigantic by comparison. It is exceptionally well kept and cared for. From the enterence to exit , the area is well marked and has excellent species of plants. Do check for timings from local contacts before going. Evenings or early morning are the best time to go.

This is a sanctuary from the delightful chaos of Kandy. Orchards, cactus, herbal garden, palm trees, fruit bats. A stunning array of trees, flowers and grasses. I spent 2.5hours here and I didn’t cover it all! A stunning experience and a must do in Kandy. Toilets well placed throughout park, you’re never too far away from one. Also NB I only experienced this once in the Plant House was a staff member pressuring me for a tip. Otherwise staff were helpful, offered advice and pointed out things of interest without a request for tips.

I was there during a sunny afternoon and enjoyed it very much. Make sure you use the entrance with the hanging bridge, much more cooler :) You don't need to be an expert about botanics to enjoy this beautiful garden. Definitely have a walk down the avenue of palm trees.

There are two entrances to the gardens one via a suspension bridge and the main entrance by Peradeniya University. We came across the bridge which has good views of the river. The gardens are just amazing, beautiful and really peaceful especially when just a short way away is the noisy bustling chaotic Kandy. There are some amazing giant bamboos, cabbage palms that form an avenue, huge java fig, enormous mahogany’s, java almond trees, flower, fern, rose gardens to name but a few. If the plants weren’t interesting enough there are hundreds of fruit bats roosting and flying about with huge wings looking more like something from a long lost era. Also plenty of cheeky Macaque monkeys. It’s just a cracking spot to chill out and take in the wonderful gardens, encompassed by the Mahaweli Ganga river.

We're not great gardeners or botanists but my two grown up sons, my husband and I thoroughly enjoyed a few hours in this magical garden.  Due to the severe downpours, we hired a buggy - what a great decision.  Our driver was so knowledgeable and informative and we definitely saw the best of the gardens (as well as having shelter from the monsoon like wind and rain!).  Highlights: fruit bats, orchid house, incredible range of trees ... definitely worth a visit.

We toured the garden one sunny afternoon and loved it so much, we came back another day to visit the glass houses during a rainy afternoon. The gardens are very well designed and kept. The glass houses are filled with so many gorgeous plants. There are a total of ten glass houses and you could easily spend a couple of hours in them.

Beautiful, peaceful stroll. We spent a couple of hours here, including a meal at the cafe, which was good.  Lots of fruit bats at the bottom end, that are on the move throughout the day - if that freaks you out, don’t go to the bottom end.  Could have spent longer here.

We loved the garden. It is very structured, beautiful, clean and big. They have signs to give you directions and they provide you with a map. It will take you and hour and half to two hours to go around the garden. It is worth visiting if you like flowers, trees and seeing landscape

An exquisite collection of Flora can be found in this vast garden (Vast according to Sri Lankan standards). The Mahaweli river circles these lush garden and there are many old trees and flowers to be found. I for one not much of an enthusiast in botany and all that jazz but I found solace in these grounds among these rare specimens of nature. There are monkeys around, don't try to feed them just observe and report. Buggies are available for the elderly but walking is the best way to experience the park. Can take 3-4 hours to properly traverse the park. There are so many pathways connecting the main trail.

visited jan 2017, 20min walk from Sarasaviuyana railway station - has an entry fee (got it in discount because of SAARC price being an Indian national) - you need the whole day to enjoy every nook and corner - There is also a suspended bridge in the premise - A tree full of the nocturnal bats who were almost awake because it was almost twilight - some huge coconuts on tiny coconut trees

There are fabulous botanical gardens about 6 km from Kandy. I have taken  a tuk tuk with a cost about 2,000 RPS a / r with (compr.  2 hours waitng) . The most interesting elements are constituted by giant bats, flowered park (next to the main entrance) and orchids' greenhouse. Inside the park you will find a restaurant, some kiosks and a coffee shop as well as a gift shop

We are keen gardeners and found this to be a beautiful and fascinating place. We were concerned as two of the four of us have difficulty walking long distances these days, but we need not have worried as we notified them and were allocated a very knowledgeable and English speaking guide and an electric buggy to take us to every corner of their many acres. It is a photographer's dream of a place with so many exotic, unique and unusual trees and plants, some of which are centuries old and from all parts of the globe. The orchid house is not to be missed. We spent a thoroughly enjoyable wholechalf day here and woukd be delighted to return..

As a gardener and plant lover, this was a beautiful and interesting experience. As someone who has done a lot of travel and seen many botanical gardens, I give it a three rating. After all, if you've visited the Singapore Botanical Gardens, you have in my opinion, seen the best you can see in tropical botanicals. The orchids are beautiful and the gardens well worth a stroll (don't forget your hat and water!). Stop off in one of the restaurants for a drink and meal. Plain Western food available for those who need a break from the delights of Sri Lankan flavours. Get yourself one of those plant identifier aps for your phone if you're a true botanist as there are some beauties here!

This is s beautifully laid out set of gardens with hot house, tropical house, orchid house at the edges then long vistas of gorgeous Sri Lankan flora, trees, roses, palms and then lovely open parkland. We spent the whole afternoon strolling around, reading the labels and enjoying the day. We visited the on site restaurant and enjoyed the buffet which has great vegetarian dishes all local and some salad. You can order plain food from the menu which is more western. There is a nice gift shop at the park entrance/exit. Reserve 2-3 hours to enjoy this at a leisurely pace.

We went to the gardens of the temple of the tooth. Made a wonderful change to the crush of people at the temple. Despite the very heavy rain storm just after we entered we loved the peaceful nature of the place. Huge number of bats and a troop of monkeys only added to the beauty of the actual gardens. The orchid house in not large but some amazing flowers with strange shapes. This is a must for anyone visiting Kandy.

I have seen these gardens before, but never had enough time to really explore the lot. So this time I took half a day (some take a whole day,) and... took a golf cart (very reasonably priced I find). One hour, including decent explananations in English by the driver.  Then, I walk to my favourite spot, the quiet southeast corner with the magnificent tree roots meandering all over the place. If you can, have a meal on the restaurant terrace (it is quickly booked) Of course, like everything in Sl the price of the gardens go up and up and up (doubles by the time you read it  haha). But it is worth the small investement, as this world renowned garden is also prefectly maintained. Something you cannot say about the Uda Watteleke behind the Temple of the tooth. A charming city park, but they could use our dear entrance fee to eliminate the killer vines that threaten this lovely but fragile ecosystem. And about the tuktuks: tried to charge me 5 times the real price (I do know my kilometers and normal price).   As the older gentleman insisted I just walked away (some honest drivers still DO exist!). Gent gave me then, a 'reasonable' price (still double, but OK). Had to be dropped off at the very special Waruna's Antique shop - a friend of mine. Tuktuk driver was really angry and tried to lure me to all kinds of 'better cheaper more serious' shops. Internally I just laughed. Was sure it was about commission - which proved to be true ;-))

Royal botanical garden must be visited if you are at Kandy. It’s very beautiful n have a very large space to slowly admire the nature. The plants and flowers are well organised n maintained. There are wide range of plants. It is a stroller friendly place. Just that it stated to rain half way, we had to go under a tree. The rain stopped within 10 mins.

You will absolutely not regret coming here, whether for the extensive and beautiful floral displays, the perfectly manicured gardens, the luxurious strolling or the ever so slightly scary walk over the small suspension bridge! We also got to see fruit bats and hummingbirds... it really was quite perfect.

Im a big nature lover and this plact hit the spot. The garden is very organized and clean. It was amazing walking around and seeing over 4000 species that are in the park. In addition to plants i got to see a bit of wildlife also which is also exciting. I highly recommend the visit.

This garden was massive and has a great range of flowers, plants and trees. You'd have to walk a lot, so if you can't I'd recommend you to use the electric cars. The place is a natural spectacle, greeny everywhere, it has a lot of really old and gigantic trees, saw some bats & monkeys around too. Half of the garden is bordered by a river which flows along the garden. The narrow suspension bridge over the river is a must see in this park, definitely a great place for family and kids.

As a family we enjoy a visit to a botanical garden in a new city we are visiting, if there is one. This one is up there with the best. Beautifully kept, some wonderful species are there. We were amazed to see the flying foxes actually flying during the daytime, so lovely to see. We saw monkeys too. There were separate houses for cacti and succulents and orchids. Only place outside of The Seychelles we have seen Coco de Mer. Nice grounds to sit and have a picnic. A lovely garden in the suburbs of Kandy, easy to get a tuk tuk. I would definitely recommend a visit.

Royal Botanic Gardens, Peradeniya are about 5.5 km to Kandy.It attracts around 2 million visitors annually.It is near the Mahaweli River (the longest in Sri Lanka).Beautiful Garden with thousands of flower species. It is renowned for its collection of orchids. Can easily spend one full day at Garden.

There is a great diversity of plants in the gardens. They are well laid out and maintained. The plan is clear if you want to follow a route and not miss anything, but it would be fine to just wander and enjoy the atmosphere. You do not need to be a keen gardener to enjoy this place.

Such a pleasant visit. We were going to skip it out due to time constraints but we are so pleased we came. Really beautiful and clean gardens where you can spend hours. Monkeys roam around too making it a fun experience! Great to escape the hustle and bustle of the city and spend a few hours in the tranquil gardens.

Spent 3 hours wandering the gardens on a fairly hot day amongst the chaos of Kandy! Gardens beautifully kept. The thousands of bats hanging in the trees was quite a sight. When we were there there was a local couple having their wedding photographs professionally shot. It’s that kind of place.

Definitely worth an hour or two to wander round these impressive gardens. The map is helpful in pointing out the different gardens and it’s all very well established and maintained. We were also entertained by a troop of monkeys who came up from the river to play in the bamboo gardens

An interesting place, with lots of variety and interest, some lovely vistas and reasonably prices eating places.  The Orchid House is always a gem, and you will never complain of Bamboo in your garden when you see the size of the ones here.  The map allows you to plan your visit and know what you are looking at.

As a horticultralist from the UK I take as many opportunities to visit botanical gardens across the globe and this has now been added to the list. A well laid out garden with majority of plants labelled. The labels are red for endemic to Sri Lanka, green for Sri Lanka and India and black for other sources. The suspension bridge is a good experience although the organisation requires some more consideration to keep queues to a minimum. The flying foxes are a true delight although they appear to take time to hone there target practice. The map is detailed and matches to the walkways and the history is a nice touch. LKR 1500 per person, we made it nearly 3 hours and felt this was good value. Well worth a trip but parking can be an issue

What a beautiful place! There were many different varieties of trees and flowers which were quite unique. It was like walking through an art gallery admiring the breathtaking works of art created by "Nature". I found this to be a refuge of peace, tranquility and serenity filled with many unique sights and sounds. From the monkeys to the hundreds of bats in the trees, this is an experience of the senses! You will be quite delighted basking in the beauty of all you see and hear!

You can hire golf buggies to get around, but these can be in short supply during busy periods and you may have to wait a while to get one. Quite well maintained gardens. You would need at least 2 hours to do justice to the Gardens. Saw quite a few unusual trees - the Kauri pines were massive.First time seeing the Maldive Coconut palms - huge coconuts. Lots of flowers and greens. Gardens were neatly laid out and the brochure was useful to help us walk about. The Laksadala shop at the exit point was an interesting shop where you can pick up a few souvenirs - reasonably priced.

Great garden and well liked after. Palms, bamboo and rainforest trees are spectacular. Orchid garden is beautiful. Well worth a visit to escape the madness of Kandy city. Give yourself a couple of hours to wonder around and have a cup of tea.

I am not a gardener or even into flowers, but this place was beautiful.    Unfortunately there when raining  and had forgotten my umbrella so cut the trip short. But huge grounds to roam around in, lots to see. I have never been impressed by orchids until the orchid house here - spectacular colours.

If you need some time for quite and reflection I recommend this place. It is easy to reach from Kandy. If you are into botanical gardens it is a jewel. If you are like me and don’t really have a touch with plants it is still a nice stroll and the suspension bridge is cool.

We spent a lovely hour and a half or so just wandering around the beautiful Royal Botanic Gardens in Kandy. It's such an oasis of calm in an otherwise busy city! Loved the Palm Avenue and the Go any Bamboo especially. The Orchid House was very nice too. Plants, trees, flowers and shrubs from all over the world with informative labelling and some nice water features. Beautifully kept lawns, in fact the whole garden is beautifully kept in every way with some nice benches scattered here and about for you to relax on and enjoy the scenery. The suspension bridge over the River gives great views and was another highlight. It only takes 6 people at a time though! A really lovely place about a half hour from central Kandy though graffic is bad at times and may nake it more.

If you have only one day in Kandy visit here first. This is an amazing garden, one of the finest in the world. Their collections are spectacular, it’s history is mind blowing, and there is something for everyone. For the thrill seaker they have a suspension bridge. The have palms, cactus, orchids, annual displays for the botanist. For the zoologist Fruit bats can be found here and are delightful. Bring water and sunscreen.

We quite enjoyed the garden, which is well laid out, quite complete and incredibly maintained.  Of particular interest is the orchid display, the medicinal garden and the beautiful annual walkway.  Having been to a number of botanical gardens in the past all over the world, this one stands out for the attention to detail combined with a great maintenance practices.  It rivals the Singapore Botanical Garden in its diversity and size. What also was impressive was the number of locals coming to visit and enjoy the space. Well worth the visit.

One of the few gardens in the whole world that got the balance right - natural vs human-intervened, old vs new, flurry of colours vs shades of green, tight spaces vs vast plains, etc. The giant century-old trees mesmerised me. I could have spend the whole day there absorbing the sights, sounds and fragrance if only there were more F&B outlets within the premise.

One of the five botanical gardens of Sri Lanka. Largest by area. Also the oldest. This area was used as the royal garden of Kandyan kings in the 18th century. Later, British government converted it to a botanical garden. Remarkably, the garden is surrounded by Mahaweli River by three sides. A fine place for nature lovers. A variety of collection of trees, flowers etc. Well maintained. Nice and calm. Access is very easy. Colombo - Kandy main road. Near Galaha junction. Public transport - Buses starting from Kandy run on this road. Need at least 2-3 hours to explore the place. May required more to observe everything. To see flowers, go to right hand side branch. Otherwise, the left hand side branch gives a true green experience. Good for spending time with family, friends, couples or even solo trips. There are monkeys. Don't feed them. Just watch their behavior. In rainy days, you need an umbrella. There are few huts as shelter. But they won't be sufficient for many people. Plenty of parking available. Vehicle are permitted inside with a fee. Cafeteria is available. Good condition. Non-commercial photography is free of charge. Don't forget to see the view of Hanthana mountain range from the garden.

There are numerous trees and shrubs planted by royalty, foreign heads of state, prime ministers and other dignitaries.  Not to be missed are the Orchid House and the huge colony of fruit bats.  Many of the plants have been imported over many years.  The palm avenue is particularly impressive.  The restaurant however is best avoided, as the food is poor quality and overpriced.

The most beautiful gardens. Photographers paradise. The colours, light, shades of green, trees, flowers, harmony, nature at its best.  The orchid house just amazing. Take time to sit and absorb this splendour. Allow plenty of time!

You get a map so you can find your way around. We did not realise you could go round in a golf cart with driver/guide, if you are not disabled. The orchids in the orchid house were varied and pretty. There is also a cactus house. The gardens are well maintained. There are flower beds and lots of trees. At one point there are thousands of flying foxes hanging in the trees.  We did not have time to go across the suspension bridge, there can be a small queue. You may see some monkeys, we did. Allow two to three hours for a good walk around.

A trip to the area around Kandy must include a visit to the Royal Botanical Gardens - although not when it's raining! The gardens must rank amongst the best in the world and are simply stunning as well as being interesting from a horticultural point of view. Don't miss the orchids but equally, do NOT miss the 22,000 flying foxes that live in the park. They made my visit!

You can spend a day here easily if you like plants. There is such a variety of plants and garden-scapes here so its worth bringing a camera. If I was going back to Kandy, I’d definitely come here. Listen for the officials blowing whistles – seems they have to stop people kissing in the park. And don’t wear a white shirt if you’re going to get serious about photographing the bats. And its inexpensive.

The botanical garden is a must see in Kandy. You can spend between 2 and 3 hours walking around. I always recommend this place to people visiting Sri Lanka. The gardens are around 5km outside of the centre of Kandy but beware trying to get there during the usual Kandy morning and afternoon rush-hours. Traffic is crazy and it could easily take you an hour to get there. These are very beautiful gardens and greenhouse with lots to see. On entry you are given a guide which clearly directs you around all of the different areas which cover more than 140 acres. The Orchid House has a collection of very beautiful orchids and the general planting displays are spectacular. There is a café for light refreshment.

We were blown away by these gardens. They are enormous and you need two or three hours to appreciate them. The orchid house was beautiful even though the guardians were very diligent. They needed to be as some tourists show no respect at all. The size of the gardens was very surprising and they were very peaceful.

What beautiful gardens and respite from the increasing traffic and pollution of Kandy. We spent about five hours strolling and relaxing in these stunning gardens set in just under 150 acres within a loop of the Mahaweli river, the longest river in Sri Lanka. Over 4000 species of plants, multiple showcase avenues of trees, gorgeous orchids, ferns, bamboo, pine collections. The bouncy suspension bridge over the river, six at a time and a man blowing a whistle to signal you to cross back over the bridge! Beautiful tropical flower and plant displays, lawns, multiple footpaths, wild macaques and huge flying foxes. We will certainly return and I could very easily have stayed until sunset. Buggy trips can be hired for RS1000 but we relished strolling around this gem. Highly recommended.

A little bit out of Kandy centre ( 400 each way in a tuk-tuk, less than 20 in a bus) these gardens are HUGe and very beautiful. So relaxing and quiet after the chaos of traffic and noise in Kandy. Take some food and water and spend a few hours here. The orchid house is stunning.

Although it's a relatively small garden, it had a fairly large selection of species and it's very well kept. The layout is charming. The orchid house and both palm drives are a must visit. Have visited many gardens during my travels, but not too many better than this.  Perhaps the highlight of our trip to Kandy and one you should not miss if visiting this City.  They are situated some 5/6K out of the town centre and are huge, covering nearly 150 acres. We were taken there by our guide, who had visited here many times, so knew where the best sights were and the optimal way to see them. Peradeniya Royal Botanical Gardens is 5km from Kandy city. It is Sri Lanka's largest Botanical Garden and is spread over 59ha (147 acres). 2-4 hours visit time recommended. Many fauna and flora photo opportunities. The Orchid House offers the visitor a captivating display of exotic blooms, good for close up photography of orchids. The fernery includes about 100 indigenous and exotic species. Spice garden, bamboo collection, plant house and cactus house are other attractions.

A must see if in Kandy Sri Lanka. Fantastic collection of orchids, wonderfully kept garden areas, great natural forest areas along the Mahaweli river on one side. What a beautiful place this is!  About 15 minutes from the centre of town in a tuk-tuk (about 300 LKR) gets you to the most beautiful gardens stuffed with gorgeous plants and flowers, all well maintained and obviously well-loved by the gardening crew. I had not visited these gardens for decades. and was gratified to see they were still beautiful and very well maintained. The Royal Botanical Gardens' is probably the best known public gardens in Sri Lanka. It sprawls over about 200 acres of lush vegetation that borders the Mahaweli river and is the ideal place for a day of relaxation with family and friends. it is just 5 km from the hill capital of Kandy and is popular with locals and tourists alike, The many greenhouses are well worth a visit. I particularly loved its beautiful collection of orchids and succulents, although the outdoor fernery could be improved with the addition of more species. Spices and medicinal plants can also be seen here. Don't forget the walk through the stately avenue of slender palm trees. Other attractions are the cannonball fruit tree, the Burma bamboo and the giant Javan fig tree. The garden boasts of over 4,000 different species of plants and more than 10,000 trees. These magnificent gardens were reserved for Kandyan royalty in days gone by. A must see if you are in the locality. It is about 20 minutes walk from the Sarasavi- Uyana (University of Peradeniya) railway station. Opening hours are from 8.00 a.m. to 5.30 p.m. daily The ticket counter closes at 5.00 p.m. As usual, foreigners pay a substantially more entrance fee when compared with the fee for local visitors - about USD 15.

Its Sri Lanka’s largest display of plant species, spread around 140 acres with over 4000 species and surrounded on three sides by Sri Lanka’s largest river Mahaweli. What not to miss: -	Double Coconut Palm trees – It’s the first set of palm trees you will see as you enter the park and walk towards your right. From the Seychelles, this palm is known to have the largest seed in the plant kingdom. Unlike other fruit bearing trees, the fruit takes around five years to mature -	The Orchid House has an attractive and mesmerizing display of flowers in full bloom. The Royal Botanical Gardens is amazing in exhibiting more than 4000 species of plants with a beautiful landscape and well maintained lawns. There are sections of Palm trees, well famous renowned Orchids, Cactus plants, Succulents, Climbers, Runners, Bushes,Shrubs, Trees, Medicinal Plants, Spices and Water Plants etc. However the ticketing gate keepers are not a match to the Royal Botanical Garden’s fame and high standards. Royal Botanical Gardens of Peradeniya is the largest one in Sri Lanka with an extent of 147 acres. You have to walk a minimum of 3 km if you want to see the gardens to a greater extent. If you wish, there are mini jeep like vehicles that would take you around, for a fee of LKR 1000. This avoids walking a long distance, tiredness and cut shorts of your time. Royal Botanic Gardens, Peradeniya are about 5.5 km to the west of the city of Kandy in the Central Province of Sri Lanka. This is the largest of the botanical gardens of Sri Lanka, It is renowned for its collection of orchids. The garden includes more than 4000 species of plants, including orchids, spices, medicinal plants and palm trees. The total area of the botanical garden is 147 acres, at 460 meters above sea level, and with a 200-day annual rainfall. The origins of the Botanic Gardens date as far back as 1371 when King Wickramabahu III ascended the throne and kept court at Peradeniya near the Mahaweli river. There is a Suspension Bridge across the River Mahaweli takes to the School of Tropical Agriculture at Gannoruwa hill. In the centre of the Gardens is an artificial lake with water plants including the giant water lily. You can visit any day to this garden. Entry fees are USD 12.50 for SARC countries and USD 25.00 for other foreign countries which seems bit expensive.

You have world renowned seed and orchid collections (not only the cheeky coco-fesse ;-). Quirky pavillions and trees with the most amazing roots, at the back is a most authentic bridge in thick rope etc etc etc etc etc. Need I say more? Sri Lanka is also a country where the young people can enjoy a romantic stroll, there is a lot of gentle babbling and smiling  going on. So (respectfully) watching the 'locals' is one of my favourite passtimes. And as lots of people speak English here, it is extremely easy to have a relaxed conversation with virtually anyone you meet. There is also a pleasant cafe-restaurant, with a nice verandah and a beautiful panorama. Those who are really adventurous may ask for a 'real curry' (spicy, as served to the locals and bus drivers ;-), and not the usual 'Baby Food' Sri Lankan cooks tend to serve to the visiting white faces ;-))

The Botanical Garden is located in Peradeniya, Sri Lanka, close proximity from Kandy. The botanical garden is 5 hours car ride from the city of Colombo. Taxi ride cost almost the same as a rental van with a driver. We paid LKR 8400 (US$ $60.00 for round trip) . You can add Pinnewala Elephant Orphanage or the Kandy temple to your itinerary. One can also take train from Colombo Fort to Kandy and then take Bus444 from Kandy clock tower to the Peraneiya Botanical Garden. You can choose Expo train, which very comfortable, clean and faster service to Kandy or the regular train ride which is cheaper and slower. The many highlights include a fine collection of orchids, roses, wide varieties of flowers, trees and ave nue of royal palm tress.  Huge Javan trees covers the lawn and gives you a feeling that you are walking through dome. Bus 644 (LKR 15) from Kandy’s clock-tower bus stop goes to the gardens. There are sign boards at the entrance to the garden gives you direction to all the attractions. There is a small restaurant inside the garden and a huge man made lake and walkway that covers the length of the lake. The weather is normally cloudy and rains intermittently most of the day, so taking an umbrella or rain coat is advisable. The weekends are always crowded and not as bad during the weekdays.  The entry fee for all foreign nationals cost LKR 3000 ( about US $21.00 depending on the exchange rate). If you'd like to eat there are several restaurants in Kandy with very reasonable prices as the food at the Botanical Garden tends to be on the high side.

The real Green Paradise of Srilanka to be seen or to be felt are: 1. Kandy to Ella train journey (Most Spectacular & Most Scenic train journey) 2. Ella (Blessed with Splendid & Mesmerising landscapes) The above two things are must if you are in Srilanka. The next real Green Paradise is in Royal  Botanical Gardens at Peradeniya in Kandy, Srilanka. It is also a must place to visit if you are in Kandy or nearby. True Lovers of Nature will find the Green Nature at its best. More than 4000 species of mind soothing & eye pleasing plants in a very very vast space. Picture speaks louder than words so please see the attached photos in this review. I also have videos of gardens (360 degree / panoramic views). Unfortunately unable to find the feature to upload videos. PS: I have also seen following botanical gardens: 1. Pamplamous Botanical Garden at Mauritius 2. Seychelles Botanical Garden on Mahe island at Seychelles 3. Valle De Mai Botanical Garden on Praslin island at Seychelles. The above 3 gardens are no where near to the Royal Botanical Garden at Peradeniya in Kandy, Srilanka in terms of Green Nature Beauty at its best. How to reach: 1. Bus: Garden is at 6 km from Kandy city. Catch bus from main city vegetable market located at 150 meter before Kandy railway station or bus stand Bus ticket less than LKR 20 2. Tuk tuk or 3 wheeler Anything in the range of LKR 300 to 500 deal is ok. There are no metered tuk tuk hence negotiate. Entrance Fee: For Asians it is LKR 1500, have passport with you. For other nationalities it is little more than it. Easy to understand garden map will be provided with ticket. Map has legends of all the places in Garden to see, small cafetaria, washrooms etc It will take 3 to 4 hours to see the Garden at your own leisure. One has to walk a lot. Timings are 8 am to 5.30 pm. Ticket counter closes at 5.00 pm. Other places to see in & around Kandy are: In Kandy City 1. Tooth Relic Temple (Dalada Maligawa): In city itself entrance fee LKR 1500 2. Kandy City Lake: In city itself, boating available at normal ticket price. 3. Gautam Buddha Idol on top of mountain. Tuk tuk will take LKR 200 from city. Around Kandy: 1. Pinnawala elephant orphanage (1 hour bus journey on route to Colombo). Enterance Fee 700 LKR for asians. For other nationalities little more. This is also a must place. Read the review of Pinnawala for detailed info. 2. Ambulwawa: a very unique temple on top of mountain at Gampola on route to Nuwara Eliya  (1 hour bus journey). Enterance ticket LKR 300 From Gampola bus stand, it will take 30 minutes to reach the temple thru hired tuk tuk. Tuk tuk 500 to 1000 LKR. 3. Aluvihara Rock Caves at Matale on route to Dambulla (1 hour bus journey). Enterance fee 500 LKR. From Matale bus stand, it is at 10 minutes drive. Tuk tuk 200 to 300 LKR. If you realy want to make your visit memorable then do: 1. Undertake train journey from Kandy to Ella (Read the review on Ella Nature Trail for detailed info) 2. Stay at Ella for couple of days & do local sightseeing in hired tuk tuk Hope, the readers will find above information useful while planning trip to Kandy in Srilanka. Wish you all the best...

The Royal Botanical Gardens is a park of Kandy situated about 5-6 km from city center in the outskirts of the Kandy. The park is spread over about 150 Acres and has nothing special except few local varieties of trees. It is a good retreat for locals during hot summers and best place for evening stroll. The ticket of the park is 1100 rupees (10 US$) per person for foreigners, which is extraordinarily high keeping in view the standard, setting and presentation of the Park. The ticket for locals is 10 rupees. There is no concession for visitors from SAARC countries.

The Royal Botanical Gardens are spread over a massive area of 147 acres and it is advisable to take a buggy if you wish to see its every nook and corner. This garden is very well maintained and houses different varieties of palms, grass, bamboo trees, king coconut trees, orchids, etc. The garden runs along the Mahaweli river and also has a suspension bridge built over the Mahaweli. There is also a memorial where famous personalities have planted trees when they have visited Sri Lanka, Queen Mary, Indira Gandhi, Yuri Gagarin to name a few. We could also locate some bats in deep slumber hanging from the pine  trees. It takes about 1-2 hours to complete the visit round the gardens.

This was an amazing garden, filled with so much history, I would highly recommend you get the shuttle, they have small and large sizes to accommodate your group, which will take you all throughout the garden, and act as a guided tour. The admissions I think is about $20 for tourists, however if you are Sri Lankan born they might give you the local price of $0.50.

Our tour guide brought us here when he decided to go 'off piste' from our itinerary.  He allocated an hour for us to have a look around, which we quickly realised would be nowhere near long enough and increased it to two hours.  You could actually spend a peaceful half day here at your leisure. The park costs next to nothing for local people but understandably tourists pay Rs1100. We were amazed by the number of unusual trees from around the world, planted by royalty and world leaders.  Then there is the huge Ficus Benjamina, a tree with large sprawling horizontal limbs.  We spent our time exploring the pathways and avenues, and the swing bridge over the river that borders the park, that allows only 6 people on at a time. There is an orchid house and a greenhouse for succulents which attracted a lot of people but we weren't overly impressed with.  There is a small visitor centre and coffee shop. I especially loved Royal Palm Avenue which is a statement piece focal point off the Great Circle Lawn.  The trees were impressive but I didn't think there was much in the way of floral planting or colour throughout the gardens.  It was an enjoyable respite during our tour.

Peradeniya  is about 5km from Kandy. It is ideally located for a visit if you are planning to get the train to Hatton (Tea Gardens) from the near bye station.  This 150 acre area has beautiful flower gardens and the small orchid house has an impressive collection. The gardens are well laid out with over 4000 species of plants and trees. I was especially impressed by the fact that most of the plants / trees are labelled. There is a large collection of trees that have been planted by a who's who of world dignitaries that have visited Srilankan over the past 100 years. Many thousands of fruit bats are nesting, hanging in trees in the arbor. Near bye is a small suspension bridge across the Mahaweli River (the longest in Sri Lanka ) which also accords great views as well. Apparently, this place attracts upwards of 2 million visitors annually and although not as grand as Kew (London) or large as Kirstenbosch (Cape Town) it certainly sets a high standard.

I have been to the gardens innumerable times but the recent visit made me realise what a gem this place is. The other two are in Hakgala and  Gampaha, though smaller, and not as well maintained are of equal merit. These gardens played an important role in establishing the value of economic and exotic plants.  Coffee, tea, rubber and many other exotic plants were introduced to the island during this time and continue to play an important role in the islands economy. Exquisitely planted and well maintained it provides an excellent day out for anybody from  courting couples to families with young children.

The Royal Botanical Gardens in Peradeniya is located in close proximity to the city of Kandy in the Central Province of Sri Lanka. It is renowned for its collection of more than 300 varieties of Orchids (not in their prime when we were there), spices, medicinal plants and palms trees. The total land extent of the botanical gardens is 147 acres, The origins of the Botanic Gardens dates as far back as 1371 when King Wickramabahu III ascended the thrown and kept court at Peradeniya near Mahaweli river.  There after the ground work for a Botanical Garden were formed by Mr Alexandar Moon in 1821. Much to our surprise we saw the giant Coco de Mer that is supposedly only found in the Seychelles; well, guess what - the Brits stole it. You definitely do not want to miss seeing this one. it can weigh 35 lbs or so. We also watched a large group of fruit bats. Overall a lovely park that should be on your list.

The great circle is a grassy central area of nearly 4 acres in extent. Around the circle is a diverse array of trees planted by dignitaries, who had visited the Peradeniya Royal Botanical Gardens. In the center of the Gardens is an artificial lake with water plants including the giant water lily & papyrus reeds. The vegetation is purely tropical, being characterized by an abundance of climbing plants or lianas, palms, bamboos, pandanus or screw-pines, epiphytes (orchids, ferns etc.), and lofty trees, the latter often having buttresses roots. The leaves are generally large, thick and leathery; the flowers usually brilliant and considerable in size, and the fruits often of immense proportions and borne on the trunks of trees or older branches.

… are truly marvellous. The sheer dimensions are breath-taking. Some of the trees are shaped as-if they had been invented by George Lucas. We saw large fruit bats, longhorns, and a sinister birdlife. Don't forget to visit the amazing orchid house.

It's very extensive. Myriad trees, plants, well-maintained beds, shrubs. You could spend a long time here without seeing it all. Although we didn't try the cafe, it looked something like decent. Really good that they had installed plenty of drinking taps, bins and toilets. Go. If you like your flora and fauna, open spaces, fab orchids, monkeys, etc. you'll love it here. I've said it would be a good rainy day activity because it'll be cooler and less busy.

It is the most popular destination of most travelers of kandy. it is almost 6 kilometers away from Kandy city and about half kilometers away from Peradeniya town. This is a one of biggest and beautiful garden in sri lanka and it will take more than 4-5 hours to visit all the places in garden.

The ticken was not expensive and there you can spend how much time you want to. Good to take some food there so you can do picnic. If not there is some shop and restaurant. Beautiful garden. Worth atraction - need to be on your list thing to do in Kandy!

This is a beautiful botanical garden where you can roam around for hours. From walking on the suspension bridge first built by the British to walking down Palm Avenue, it's best to enjoy in the morning whilst the weather is cool. A personal highlight was the orchard house - stunning orchards. Avoid the plant house though as some man lured us in trying to show us the different plants then wanted 200 rupees for his trouble; don't think so.

If you come to Kandy you must not miss tha Royal Botanical park. It is supremely relaxing. For £6 each you are treated to a horticultural ballet of scenic splender, great colour, and fascinating plants and trees. The price includes a plan of the gardens which is easy to follow and takes the walker through different pockets of garden rooms with powerful and elegant mature trees open park land,palm groves and seasonal planted areas. To complement all this are specific houses that have tropical plants,special ferns and orchids. It's a gardeners dream, a lovers stroll in paradise for just six quid. It took my wife and I two hours to gently stroll around the park with a 30 min stop for afternoon tea, which was well worth the £20 that we paid.

1100 rupees is not expensive for entry to this garden, which has a large and varied collection of plants and trees. Our particular highlights were the Double Coconut, Giant Bamboo and the Orchid House (which was beautiful). We spent 90 minutes here and walked about 75% of it, but didn't stop too much. Beware the gardeners after tips, we were caught by one who had captured a scorpion, as soon as we looked at it he was after tips! A very pleasant place to spend an hour or two.

The gardens are stunning and lovely walk around for a couple of hours. They give you a good map when you enter. They tried to short change us at the ticket office so check your change carefully! Plus the ticket price is a little steep for tourists on a tight budget at 1100 rupees. Bring food as the restaurant there is very overpriced. Easy accessible by bus from the centre (clock tower) of Kandy

Although unfortunately it was raining during our visit, the botanical gardens are well worth a visit whilst in Kandy. You can spent the afternoon walking around the gardens, with a beautiful array of plants trees and flowers on display. There is also a nice restaurant/cafe in the grounds.

We came back to the botanical gardens after couple of years and since we have been a bit short on time we decided to take a ride on the electric shuttle which includes a guide as well. Driving around in that we covered the garden within about 2 hours and had lots of chances to take plenty of photos. Since we came with kids they also enjoyed the visit due to the fact that we took the electric shuttle. You can easily spend the whole day here. For sure we will come here again and take a long walk like during our first visit.

While the green house is very beautiful with many exotic plants it isn't on the same page as that in the Botanic Gardens in Singapore however the overall experience of a Botanic Garden with huge mature trees and palm lined avenues and artificial lakes is world class.  Very pleasant place for a picnic, stoll and general relaxation.

I didn't expect to find the gardens that interesting but was amazed at the wonderful trees and plants which created a sense of calm and wellbeing as we wandered about. There was always an unexpected item of interest to see - an African sausage tree, a tree planted by Yuri Gagarin, absolutely massive bamboos, the impressive Palm Avenue.  I found the most fascinating trees were the giant figs trees growing out of each others' roots. (see photo)  There were also the orchid and cactus houses, both containing impressive collections. The whole place was obviously looked after with such care - it must require endless work to keep it under control. It was a pity about the groups of people haring around in golf carts - they must have missed so much!

Beautiful peaceful gardens on the outskirts of kandy a lovely way to spend a few hours away from the hustle and bustle of the city.Beautiful orchids and the giant bamboo trees you have to see to believe.A lot of newly wed couples have there wedding photos done there.

the finest of its kind in Asia, the largest of the botanical gardens of Sri Lanka,The town of Peradeniya is located at a distance of 110km from Colombo There are around ten thousand plants & trees inclusive of 4000 labeled species. Beautiful gardens to walk around and look at the various trees and plants. Even though it was quite busy it was quite and peaceful. My favourite places/views where the Royal Palm Avenue, Memorial Trees and the Orchid House. If you enjoy gardening and plants this is well worth a visit.

This garden has a large collection of plants, more then 4.000 species and is beautifully maintained. Highlights for me were the impressive palm avenues, the huge fig tree in the middle of the lawn, the fernery and the giant bamboo of Burma. There is a restaurant with a roofed verandah were you can enjoy a drink of lunch with a nice view of the great lawn.  Entrance is 1.1000 LKR.   Highly recommended.
