We spent a very pleasant couple of hours walking around the grounds and enjoyed a light lunch at the cafe.  The orchids were especially beautiful, and it was nice to see that the gardens are enjoyed by the locals as much as the tourists.

My husband and I visited the gardens as part of a four day tour we had booked through Hayes and Jarvis called "Cultural Kandy and Tea." I'm not sure what I was expecting, however I was simply overawed when we arrived. There are so many varieties of plants, trees, flowers etc, many of which are so big I felt like Alice in Wonderland as we walked around! We would recommend taking a decent camera as there is so much to look at. Our guide told us we had an hour to look around, but we could have spent at least double that time; as we reached the hour mark, we realised there was another section we hadn't even looked at and so we ended up trying to get around it quite quickly, but you could easily spend a good morning here. We would highly recommend visiting the gardens, one of the most beautiful places we have ever seen.

I think this is a must visit. Huge gardens with over 4000 species of plants and trees, including g over 140 different types of orchids. It takes around two hours to walk round, but for those less able there are golf buggies to hire for around £5 and this includes a guide. There is also see a large array of wildlife. The one thing that did spoil it a bit was in certain areas people had been having picnics and left their rubbish.

We added the botanical gardens to our tour of Kandy and were able to enjoy a peaceful break from the hustle and bustle of this busy city. The gardens are beautifully maintained and a haven of peace and tranquility. Definitely worth a visit

Lovely botanical gardens which were a relaxing change from the chaos of Kandy. A nice guide leaflet given at the entrance which was not usual around Sri Lanka. Far more interesting then I would have thought and a very tranquil stroll. No idea of the cost as our guide paid.

It’s a big place. We took 3 hours to go around. We didn’t go into all different greenhouses and didn’t see all the different trees, flowers or plants in the park. If you want to see all of it you need more time. The place is very beautiful, peaceful, wonderful landscapes and amazing flowers/trees/plants. Have been here 3 times and would go back again as everytime I go I see something new. The photos speak for themselves! Keep an eye out for the monkeys near the bamboo trees and the beautiful rainbow eucalyptus tree native to Hawaii! Gorgeous!

We paid an entrance fee of LKR 1100 per person. Given the expanse of the place I can understand why the entrance fee is high. The gardens are breathtakingly beautiful and well maintained. An abundance of trees, flowers, shrubs etc from around the world in a variety of settings. Tranquility in abundance, beauty everywhere, plus wildlife surprises including monkeys and fruit bats. And a superb café overlooking an enormous lawn. Nature lovers will enjoy this place!

My first thoughts on it was just a normal garden with trees and flowers. When we arrived and was told to pay LKS1100 for the entrance fee, I was flabbergasted. However I must say it was worth every rupee paid. Other than a very educational tour of the entire neatly planned garden, we photographed many interesting trees and plants which we have not seen before. The tuk tuk driver told us we would need around 2 hours in teh garden but in the end it took us 3 hours as it started to rain and we took shelter in The Royal Garden Cafe situated right in the centre of the park. It was the best decision ever as we had the best Sri Lankan rice and curry set meal in our entire trip. Every dish that came with the set was cooked to perfection as most dishes we have tasted so far during our trip were always too salty. The prices for the food and drinks are reasonable too. When the rain stopped we continued our exploration to the Flower Garden and Orchid House. However the Flower Garden has just been replanted so not much flowers were seen and the Orchid house had just basic orchid plants. I have seen many more better Orchid houses in Singapore and Malaysia. However the Palm and Bamboo garden and many other flowering trees were fascinating to view.

Simply stunning park and gardens and by far the best thing we did in Kandy. With limited time we opted for a golf cart tour which was well worth the money, extremely knowledgeable and patent guide who made lots of photo stops and took us to the far corners of the garden that I'm sure we would have otherwise missed. We visited on International children's day and the park was filled with the sounds of happy kids having a great time, it also made for a wonderful sight seeing them all playing and madly waving at us as we cruised by. Another magic Sri Lankan experience.

This is a very large space - we could have spent more than the two hours we had. Magnificent trees and shrubs plus a couple of specialist enclosure for orchids and cacti. The labelling of specimen trees is not the best and often completely missing but this does not detract from the beauty  of the place. Plenty of facilities in the gardens (cafe and loos) make it a very relaxing experience after the hectic nature of Kandy just a couple of miles away.

We had a stop at the botanical gardens on our itinerary and didn't know much about it before we arrived but it is well worth a stop. We wandered around for a couple of hours, worth taking comfy shoes and some water although there is quite a lot of shade. Definitely bring your camera as the grounds are beautiful and there is lots of wildlife to take photos of! We also stopped at the little stand selling ice cream and drinks, it was very cheap (£0.20) for an ice cream which seemed very good considering it's a tourist attraction. The toilets were clean and western style ( but worth bringing your own toilet roll!).

It's a nice place to drop by to enjoy nature in Kandy. The weather is cooler than in the lowlands but it still gets hot near midday so going earlier might have been better for my group. The entrance fee is 1100rupees per person. There are golf carts that ferry people around the garden faster but we opted to walk. It's a big place so the one hour we allotted for it simply wasn't enough. Give it at least 2-3 hours to just have a leisurely stroll around.

I spent half a day wandering the botanical gardens, which are huge and full of lots of different flora and fauna to see. An oasis of green peace in the outskirts of Kandy, and well worth a visit. The original garden was modelled on Kew, and there is an army of gardeners (in khaki fatigues, but with wellies) who keep it looking fantastic. Highlight for me was probably the collection of huge Ficus, but there is enough to amuse most people. Only gripe is that the signage isn't great; a few huge trees were unmarked, and the common names were often missing. Well worth a visit.

Very relaxing, many varieties of trees, plants and flowers from all over the world, Worth a visit if you are in Kandy. Downside is parking difficulty and shelter during rains. Needs more improvement to cater to the high number visiting the gardens.

A beautiful place for a leisurely walk, and beautifully landscaped. Amazing collection of trees and shrubs. Started and used as the pleasure gardens of the King's of Kandy, it also features in the film "Bridge on the River Kwai". Must visit if you are in Kandy.

We visited around 3pm- fairly busy around the entrance but easy to get tickets. We entered the gardens and sauntered around the different parts.  It was spread out so didn't seem crowded as paths wide. Each tree has a name plaque and they are arranged in groups Eg: bamboo forest.  Vast array of botanical specialities with lots of benches around for a stop. Flowers were colourful and gardens appeared well kept yet we didn't see any gardeners. We stopped mid walk for an ice cream in the shop. Fairly cheap and also sold drinks & snacks.  We crossed the large central grassy area to sit under the central tree as the were no benches near the tea shop. Overall very pleasant afternoon spent nearly 2hours wondering around. Gift shop at exit bit pricey, didn't purchase anything but they had a wide range. Would definitely return.

The botanical gardens is a well preserved 59 hectares land and there is a lot to see. There's flora from all around the world and very well maintained. I recommend going there earlier (they open by 7:30 am) so its not very hot and there's not a lot of people. There are also a few animals around like fruit bats, crows and other birds. We had an enjoyable walk around the gardens. As we were walking around, we noticed a lot of couples doing wedding shoots there. I'm not surprised as the landscape is really beautiful!

Don't forget to allocate at least 3 hours in the day for this brilliant location in the heart of the beautiful city of Kandy. I was pretty excited the previous day thinking Botanical Garden would typically be a house to colorful and brilliant flowers only to be mighty surprised to visit a garden spread over 140 acres of land with a plethora of plantation ranging from orchids, palm ranges, plant ranges, age old tree species and fernery to spice and medicinal gardens. A serious recommendation for all photography buffs to carry the best lens possible because rest assured you're going to get a few shots which are worth printing and preserving for posterity. The suspension bridge at the other end of the garden certainly is fun and rejuvenating. P.S.> Do be prepared for at least 3-5kms of walking around and suggest to explore by yourselves with the map provided at the entrance - The element of surprise keeps you going and on the high until you finish the long tour by foot. It's definitely worth the time and effort!

Great way to spend a few hours.  The suspension bridge is fun and the bird life good.  Never seen so many bats flying during the day, they were being attacked by crows.  The orchid house has some amazing orchids.  Altogether very nicely laid out and relaxing.

Beautifully maintained, these gardens are like a tropical paradise with wonderful vistas over green lawns and shady trees.  We loved our wander around and seeing monkeys playing in a hedge maze. Restaurant food was a bit disappointing - but the views from the veranda were lovely.

You could spend a whole day here - it is a superb botanical garden with lots of places to just hang out and chill. Take a small ruck-sack with some snacks and water (bring your rubbish back) Avoid the heat of the day Take an umbrella - always... Excellent Lavazza Espresso in the shop at the exit

We were told before going that it was not worth the 1100 LKR to get in. We decided to try it out anyway and we were not disappointed. We loved it here. So relaxing, calm, large and very well maintained. What a great little surprise in the middle of a hectic city. There is such a variety of plants and even some surprising animals (Bats and Monkeys). Such a pretty and relaxing way to spend the morning. I would recommend the morning to go - It did start to heat up quite a bit by the time we left at about 11.

Definitely go even if you're not into gardens!  This place is magical.  We have been 2 times and it really is an amazing place.  So much to see from all over the world.  Don't touch the bamboo as leaves little splinters… that goes for all the bamboo in Sri Lanka!

Royal Botanical Garden, Peradeniya is situated about 5.5 km to the west from the city of Kandy in the Central Province of Sri Lanka and attracts 2 million visitors annually. It is renowned for its collection of a variety of orchids. It includes more than 4000 species of plants, including of orchids, spices, medicinal plants and palm trees. Attached to it is the National Herbarium of Sri Lanka. The total area of the botanical garden is 147 acres (0.59 km2), at 460 meters above sea level, and with a 200-day annual rainfall. It is managed by the Division of National Botanic Gardens of the Department of Agriculture.

The Botanical Garden (Kandy), the Rock in Sigiriya, Polonnaruwa, Dambulla Caves, and Minneriya National Park - and definitely for the teenagers was white-water rafting (just 2 hours from Kandy) were top of our list of things we saw in Sri Lanka.

Also, there is a giftshop that you go through when leaving. There are some lovely souvenirs there and not expensive either.

As a member of kew gardens in London I always try to visit other Botanic Gardens on my travels. This is probably the best I've seen so far! It's a beautifully kept place and has a vast array of trees and plants both native to Sri Lanka and from far flung places. There were also bats, chipmunks and monkeys who love to get their pictures taken! The staff are all very friendly and helpful. I'd say the cafe is ok but you might want to buy your own sandwiches beforehand and have a picnic (just be prepared if it starts to rain!) We just had a super afternoon here. Pretty reasonable price: rs1100 per adult I think, and don't worry you'll get you monies worth. There are a number of out houses displaying orchids, ferns, general plants, cacti amongst many others. The loos are ok, there were cleaners onsite but they still smelt a little, not horrendously though. Some of the cubicals only have a hole, others have a toilet, don't just think there are only holes, check before entering :) We had a walk down right to the end where there's a roundabout type place on the map - at the end of the main path, not 'The Great Circle'. We saw what I think was an eagle (it was a massive bird of prey whatever it was, just got away before I got a clear look), a metre long lizard type creature, many huge bats hanging in the trees and flying about (all high up so don't panic!), monkeys and horned cows - amongst many beautiful plants, trees and lined avenues. The flower gardens on the way back were particularly stunning. We spent probably 1h 30m, if you're really interested in plants and fauna you'll want longer...for us a walk around, spotting the various creatures and appreciating the scenery didn't take longer. On exiting the security will more than likely suggest that the only exit is through the gift shop, of course it's not, there's one just to the left of it! We were going to grab a coffee from the cafeteria in the shop however if you exit and to the right just 20metres away there's a corner shop type place called Royal Mall - that serves drinks, food etc, much cheaper than the cafeteria and better choice - it's also rated pretty high on TripAdvisor...there's an ATM here too.

After our tour around the Cultural Triangle of Sri Lanka, my husband and I visited these gardens on our way back to our resort.  It was absolutely beautiful!  It puts Kew Gardens to shame!  The whole gardens are immaculately kept, so clean, so well signed and the layout with a lake in the centre is beautiful.  You cannot get away from the magical smells of exotic trees, the flowers from the cannonball trees are the most fragrant we have encountered!  The huge rain trees are spectacular as are the giant bamboos! This is where you can see the magnificence of Sri Lanka's tropical plants all in one place.  My husband wasn't keen to visit here, thinking it would be a few plants here and there and green houses, but it turned out to be the best surprise ever!  We both loved it, spent 3 hours here and probably would have stayed longer if we had had time.  The orchids are all in a green house and a very large selection.  There was a gardener who showed us different spice trees and nuts to try, and even cut us some cinnamon leaves and stalks.  We saw fruit bats fly overhead and land in the large palms.  There is a large river that runs alongside the gardens and it has an adventurous rope style bridge you can walk across the river on.  We went on a Saturday but it was still calm and peaceful.  If you like flora, you will absolutely love this place.

At the far end we were absolutely amazed at the number of bats - thousands upon thousands in the trees.  Probably part of the reason we weren't bothered by mosquitoes, flies or any insects. This is situated in the heart of Peradeniya quite close to the university and the Peradeniya rest house. Parking is on the road so rather tough to find a parking spot. Entrance is Rs.50 for a local and Rs.1100 for a foreigner which is a rather huge disparity. All who pay the ticket price for a foreigner get a map of the garden while the local ticket did not get a map. Opening hours are 7.30AM to 5.00PM. Room for improvement in the signage inside the garden to enable visitors to ensure all areas of the garden are covered. You will find a lot of families with kids & couples in the park specially on weekends. There are 2-3 carts available with a driver that takes you around for an hour for a fee. The history of the garden dates back to 1371 and it was limited to royalty. The highlights are the Royal palm avenue, Double Coconut avenue, the orchid house and the giant fig tree. There is a spice garden & giant bamboo trees as well. Ample space to just sit and enjoy the beauty around you. It is well maintained although he descriptions of the flora & fauna should be more visible.

This park covers 147 acres and has a history dating back to 1371. There are people who complain about the price to go into the Gardens and yes, like all places in Sri Lanka we pay more than the locals do and we are not used to paying at home. Kandy botanical garden is a nice park for locals to have a walk and a picnic on a day off, and learn some plants names meanwhile. As for the tourist, especially the one that has been in large and well-maintained botanical gardens in Europe or America, this is not a very entertaining or educative place, and neither is a good picnic place, considering the tourist ticket price of Rs 1100. The grounds are, also, not sufficiently clean, with empty bottles and food package seen in some places - not sure, whether these are the traces of the day's picnickers, or leftovers of the previous days. All that said, as in any park around the world, one'll definitely find some pleasant and beautiful places to sit and relax, and some nice photo opportunities. Orchids pavilion also seemed quite small and monotonous - I was more impressed by variety and colors of wildly growing orchids in Thailand. Beware of people who come up and tell you the name of the plant you are looking at (many plants are not clearly signed), and suggest to show you a spider/flower/whatever nearby, and demand money afterwards - more than you are willing to pay for such a small "service".

I visited the Gardens with work colleagues. We were in Kany for a meeting and the deal was: we have to work from past noontime till late in the evening to make up for the wonderful morning break to see this breathtaking place.  And indeed, we struck a very good deal. The Royal Botanical Garden, Peradeniya is situated about 5.5 km to the west from the city of Kandy in the Central Province of Sri Lanka. Its history goes as far back as 1371 under the pre-colonial kingdoms of Sri Lanka. The idea of a botanical garden was formed during the British colonial period and groundwork started in 1821. Formally established in 1843 with plants brought from Kew Garden, Slave Island, Colombo, and the Kalutara Garden in Kalutara, it now attracts 2 million visitors annually and is renowned for its collection of a variety of orchids. It includes more than 4000 species of plants, including of orchids, spices, medicinal plants and palm trees. Attached to it is the National Herbarium of Sri Lanka. Give yourself a good 3 to 4 hours to really appreciate the beauty of this place.  Guided tours are offered with a botanist who knows his plans and garden like the palm of his hand. The Garden is a favorite location for wedding photos and  on a nice sunny weather - one gets the bonus of seeing a traditional  Sri Lankan wedding entourage - with the bride , groom and entourage in  their colorful wedding costumes.

Recently I visited this garden with my group. The garden having approximately area of 230 Hectors and completed in the British regime around 100 years back. If you wish to visit all parts of the garden then I am sure it will take minimum two days. Hence we visited most popular and signature attractions. We started with Herbal plant section where spice trees such as nutmeg, clove, and cardamom trees are well planted. Surprisingly I have seen a plant of Camphor for the first time in my life. Usually we make camphor by chemical combinations, artificially however the plant here having the leaves same aroma like artificial camphor...isn't surprising? Then we visited Orchid section where more than 25 different species are planted in an environment which is suitable to grow for these plants. Later we visited VIP section where there were special plants which were planted by various famous personalities such as Late Prime Minister of India Smt.Indira Gandhi, first astronaut in the world Mr. Yuri Gagarin, First Prime minister of Vietnam Mr. Dong etc. Double coconut or Seashell coconut and the elephant foot like willow tresses are some plants you will never find anywhere. Even I have seen on plant having a poisonous bark, the juice of the same was used in olden days for dipping the arrow of bows for wild animal hunting. When I asked the botanical name of this tree my guide exclaimed "Mother-in laws-tongue" hahaha...Last but not least Bamboo plantation area was well preserved. Overall the garden is very beautiful and maintained very nicely. I am very sure everybody will rejuvanate after visiting this garden.

The Guide Map and information pamphlet given to all visitors says that the history of these gardens go as far back as 1371 and that the Kandyan kings established a Royal Garden and residence and temple in the18th century. The buildings and gardens were destroyed during the British conquest of the last Kandyan king in 1815. The present gardens were established by the new colonial government just six years later to cultivate economic plants such as coffee, pepper, cardamom, nutmeg and cinnamon. These and several other spices thrive in the Spice Garden section today. Over the next 150 years the gardens grew in size and importance becoming an internationally respected scientific institution with a wide variety of indigenous and exotic economic and medicinal plants. Today the garden’s 147 acres contain more than 4000 species of plants and provide a haven of tranquility amidst the hustle and bustle of noisy Kandy. The vast lawns, majestic avenues, breathtaking floral displays, wide spreading trees, lake, orchids, ferns and well maintained paths and byways provide a respite for more than 2 million visitors each year and is a popular outing for courting couples, families and tourists alike. Even the dogs seemed to be lulled into a soporific torpor. During this visit we spent just over an hour and a half and had it not been for the impending rain would have stayed much longer. The peace, beauty and grandeur combine to provide an excellent location for some meditative recharging of both body and soul. The £5.50 entrance fee is money well spent.

There are more different palms (species, sizes, shapes, colours) than you ever guessed would exist; and the same goes for the orchid collection; fig trees which strangle their hosts (nature is cruel); a colonial style lawn; amorous young couples; a suspension bridge over the river which is especially fun to walk across together with a bunch of boisterous teenage students (don't worry: a fiercely- looking friendly guard will see to that the bridge doesn't get over- loaded); a large colony of fruit bats in one of the palm alleys; zebu cattle (when did you last time visit a botanical garden with free- roaming cows?);  and of course all the plants from around world. And birds galore, too! There are ample good toilets and drinking water fountains, a cafeteria and a restaurant (which we didn't visit). Come early if you can before it gets too hot. I used to be a botanist and horticulturist some years ago, so visited quite a few botanical gardens. Peradeniya Garden compares very favourably, probably one of the nicest gardens I have visited, perhaps with the exception of Kew and Edinburgh RBGs - but of cause the flora is completely different here. I visited a few times during my 3 months stay in nearby Pilimathalawa, and every time found something new to enjoy. Various tree collections are especially impressive; there are not as many herbaceous plants as you would see in a temperate botanic garden (I guess maintenance of herbaceous borders in a tropical climate would be a bit of a nightmare!) Orchid house was a bit ordinary, mostly with the Phalaenopsis which is so common as a houseplant nowadays, but still laid out nicely. The entrance fee is significantly higher for foreign tourists than for local people (which I think is quite reasonable, as it is still much cheaper for westerners than any of the major European botanic garden) - beware that the website may not have an up-to-date price on it. The entrance fee for foreigners at the time of writing (March 2013) is 1100 Sri Lankan rupees. The cafeteria is overpriced in comparison with other food outlets outside of the garden; food is OK but not particularly inspiring.

The Royal Botanical Gardens of Peradeniya is situated about 5.5 km to the west from the city of Kandy in the Central Province of Sri Lanka and attracts 1.2 million visitors annually. It is renowned for its collection of a variety of orchids. It includes more than 300 varieties of orchids, spices, medicinal plants and palm trees. Attached to it is the National Herbarium. The total area of the botanical garden is 147 acres (0.59 km2), at 460 meters above sea level, and with a 200-day annual rainfall. It is managed by the Division of National Botanical Gardens of the Department of Agriculture. The origins of the Botanical Gardens date as far back as 1371 when King Wickramabahu III ascended the throne and kept court at Peradeniya near Mahaweli river. This was followed by King Kirti Sri and King Rajadhi Rajasinghe. A temple was built on this location by King Wimala Dharma, but it was destroyed by the British when they were given control over the Kingdom of Kandy. Thereafter, the groundwork for a botanical garden was formed by Alexandar Moon in 1821. The Botanical Garden at Peradeniya was formally established in 1843 with plants brought from Kew Garden, Slave Island, Colombo, and the Kalutara Garden in Kalutara. The Royal Botanical Garden, Peradeniya was made more independent and expanded under George Gardner as superintendent in 1844.On his death in 1849 George Henry Kendrick Thwaites became superintendent. The Garden came under the administration of the Department of Agriculture when it was established in 1912. The classical Avenue of Palms is located in this Garden. One tree with a significant history is the Cannonball Tree planted by King George V of the United Kingdom and Queen Mary in 1901. The tree is bent with its fruits, which look like cannonballs. During the Second World War, the Botanical Garden was used by Lord Louis Mountbatten, the supreme commander of the allied forces in the South Asia, as the headquarters of the South East Asia Command.
